Standard: Compartments not continuously occupied by crewmembers (e.g., cargo compartments, lavatories, galleys, partitioned-off crewmember rest areas) include fire detection and extinguishing and automated suppression system features required to mitigate the risk of fire presented by the design and approved cargo types in each compartment. Fires are detected and flight crew are notified within 60 seconds of the fire starting. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Inspect design requirements to verify approved cargo types and crewmember requirements to determine occupiable compartments that do not have a crewmember present to monitor for smoke/fire.
(2) Inspect design documentation to verify fire detection and fire extinguishing or automated fire suppression requirements have been determined for each occupiable compartment that does not have a crewmember present to monitor for smoke/fire.
(3) Inspect design and operational documents to show that firefighting procedures have been determined for each occupiable compartment that does not have a crewmember present to monitor for smoke/fire.
(4) Inspect design documents to verify fire detection and fire extinguishing or automated fire suppression systems are installed in each occupiable compartment that does not have a crewmember present to monitor for smoke/fire. Analysis.
  (1) Perform analysis that shows the fire detection features of the system are able to detect fires in each occupiable compartment that does not have a crewmember present to monitor for smoke/fire within 60 seconds so that flight crew actions may be performed to mitigate the fire before it causes damage to flight-critical systems or structure, or spreads to additional areas or cargo.
  (2) Perform analysis that shows fire extinguishing or automated fire suppression systems provide required agent concentration in all compartment locations for the required time to extinguish fire for typical and worst-case cargo loading configurations and conditions. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Perform lab testing that shows the fire detection features of the system are able to detect fires within 60 seconds so that flight crew actions may be performed to mitigate the fire before it causes damage to flight-critical systems or structure, or spreads to additional areas or cargo.
    (2) Lab test: Perform lab testing that shows fire extinguisher or automated fire suppression systems provide required agent concentration in all not continuously occupied compartment locations for the required time to suppress fire for typical and worst-case cargo loading configurations and conditions.
    (3) Ground test: Perform ground test to show each fire detection circuit can be checked for function on the ground.
    (4) Ground test: Perform ground testing that shows the fire detection features of the system are able to detect fires within 60 seconds so that flight crew actions may be performed to mitigate the fire before it causes damage to flight-critical systems or structure, or spreads to additional areas or cargo.
    (5) Ground test: Perform ground testing that shows fire extinguishing and automated fire suppression systems provide required agent concentration in all not continuously occupied compartment locations for the required time to suppress fire for typical and worst-case cargo loading configurations and conditions. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (6) Flight test: Perform flight test to show each fire detection circuit can be checked for function in flight.
    (7) Flight test: Perform flight testing that shows the fire detection features of the system are able to detect fires within 60 seconds so that flight crew actions may be performed to mitigate the fire before it causes damage to flight-critical systems or structure, or spreads to additional areas or cargo.
    (8) Flight test: Perform flight testing that shows fire extinguishing or automated fire suppression systems provide required agent concentration in all compartment locations for the required time to suppress fire for typical and worst-case cargo loading configurations and conditions.
